content.comment_body: I'm new to [product_name] and AWS. After weeks of attempts and searching forum posts, I'm still unable to make my [product_name] app connect to my device in the AWS cloud. Locally, it works well, but after transferring to the cloud environment, connection fails. I've ensured I'm running the latest [product_name] and [product_name] versions, set up clock synchronization, matched AWS regions, configured cloud transfer settings, tested online connectivity, and set up IoT tags in the app. Any ideas on what I could be missing? My [product_name] password is [product_name]. Thank you.
I have the same issue. No one seems willing or able to help, and I'm even open to paid advice but still nothing.
Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Please note this is an English-speaking forum; kindly post in English. Thank you.

I've tried changing both app and AWS thing regions, but the [product_name] app doesn't connect to my device functions. The interface just spins without activating the expected function. In various examples, inputs like I1 and I2 are used, but my [product_name] app only allows push buttons and network input(V) in cloud mode. If someone could try the Test.zip example I posted and share feedback, it would help greatly. Please help, thank you.

I can't identify the issue precisely. I tested your [product_name] diagram and your app on my device, but could not connect to the web server. However, when I created a new project (Test_2), it worked fine.

Thank you for reviewing my problem. The diagrams look the same and Test2 resembles my app closely, except it lacks IoT tags. How did you deploy it to the AWS cloud? Did you remove tags and IoT entries before sharing it? Thanks again.

I've never used AWS cloud; I avoid it because of the requirement for credit card information at registration. I only tested your projects locally on my device and web server. Your app keeps loading endlessly, so I created a fresh [product_name] project (Test_2) without any IoT tags. With this setup, accessing the web server worked without problems.

Thank you. My [product_name] app works with the local web server, but the AWS cloud connection fails. I would appreciate help from anyone experienced with AWS cloud integration for [product_name]. Thank you.
I'm surprised the official support account from [company_name] hasn't commented on this. It raises questions about the account's purpose.
Sadly, this is a feature that isn't currently supported.

Who said that was the case? [company_name] developed and sells the product; claiming non-support for a key feature promoted during release seems odd. The lack of supportive replies from the official account is notable. By the way, I've described the device as similar to Arduino class tech on a DIN rail. As if by coincidence, a recently advertised device on Arduino's site now offers cloud computing—something [company_name] hasn't delivered for their product in over three years.

Thank you for sharing your thoughts. If you believe it's a mistaken comment, could you explain why my app doesn't function in AWS? As mentioned, I'm new to the platform and would appreciate expert insight. For reference, [company_name] support clarified that assistance beyond downloading the app into AWS isn't covered. Even that needed specific versions and workarounds. Would you be willing to help?

You're asking in the wrong place. It's unhelpful of [company_name] support to deny responsibility for a marketed feature. Initially, I experimented with AWS and got partial results, but the connection failed over time. After stepping away, AWS prompted me about payment after the free trial expired. You can experiment, but most here have likely given up on AWS cloud connectivity for this product. It's not sustainable due to possible changes in rules and APIs, and [company_name] claims it's outside their remit.

My apologies. Frustration got the better of me. Unfortunately, it seems [company_name] has partnered with AWS for this feature, leading customers to ongoing frustration. The time spent troubleshooting has resulted in monthly AWS charges, which I'm willing to pay for a working system. I've enlisted AWS support as a last attempt and hope someone at [company_name] is aware of these issues, finding solutions or moving towards a more reliable cloud environment. Please don't discontinue [product_name] and access.
Thank you for mentioning the Arduino Opta—it looks promising. Hopefully [company_name] is paying attention.
Useful information on registering and configuring AWS Cloud for [company_name] [product_name].
Registering with AWS and connecting through [product_name].

Thank you, [user_name]. I followed all the steps outlined in the links provided by [company_name], but it still doesn't work. My device connects correctly to the cloud, with the shadow displaying my data transfer items. AWS support confirmed my application's deployment and environment creation worked without error, but they're unsure of the problem. They are now reviewing logs. Once I receive a response, I'll submit another support request to [company_name] with AWS findings. For my AWS app, I used only a portion of the example program to avoid errors, and it works fine locally. The complete example, however, shows the same cloud issue: function keys in the deployed app just spin. Attached are my shadow file and copies of the programs if you'd like to help.

Your latest upload has the same issue with the [product_name] project. Regardless of browser, I cannot reach the web server. In my opinion, something is wrong with your [product_name] project. See attached video.

Thank you for your feedback. The [product_name] app is intended for cloud use. As you don't use it on AWS, did you modify the app for local deployment before installing? Otherwise, the functions target the cloud and won't work locally. Please clarify. I watched your mp4 video; though mostly in German and without captions, I understood to check for proxy or security interference. I've verified no proxy and disabled antivirus but still have the same cloud failure. I'll reinstall [product_name] updates afresh and retry cloud setup.

I made no changes to the [product_name] project. As mentioned, I'm not convinced by the cloud concept, especially regarding AWS connection. Amazon requests card info for even a free account, claiming it's just for verification. Neither [company_name] nor AWS provide real assistance, or perhaps aren't willing to. Therefore, I can't help further. Sorry.

Thank you for replying; no need to apologize. I appreciate your effort. Now I see why my program doesn't run for you. The test programs from the zip file need to be tailored for the specific local or cloud settings (IP, subnet, gateway), otherwise they won't work. I'm committed to solving the cloud issue or helping [company_name] address the bug. Thanks again.

To further diagnose, could someone visit the link below and report the response? This is a simple cloud demo included in my test.zip file. [url] Clicking the start-stop checkbox doesn't activate in the cloud, but works locally. If it works for others, I'll know the problem is on my side. Also, AWS support asked me to check my [product_name] application and access logs, but I can't find access.log or know where it's stored. Any advice? Thank you.
What is the password?
Password is [product_name], all uppercase.

Hi, I have some experience connecting [product_name] to AWS. I followed examples from [company_name] and customized them. Where exactly are you stuck? Do you have compatible hardware? Is your AWS account set up? Did you define variables for cloud connection, register your device, set up the AWS environment, and load the page built in [product_name]? Are the rules and policies properly defined? Let me know and I'll share my experience.
I've tested it, but no result. See attached video.
Thank you. This is the same response I get with all my [product_name] cloud apps, even official training examples. Your help is very much appreciated.

Quick update: I spent over two hours in a Microsoft Teams call with a support engineer from [company_name]. After trying everything, including rewriting the app, the problem remained. The issue is not related to the app or diagrams, so it's now referred to [company_name]'s R&D. I moved the programs to another PC to rule out system issues—same cloud result. I recently noticed my root user's region differs from my IAM user's region. I deploy using IAM, and thought differing regions wouldn't matter as long as the ones used in the app and device match. I'll test aligning them after the holidays. Any thoughts?
Meant 'would not matter' in the previous post.

It seems many of us are stuck, with little technical support. It's a classic case of two large companies (one making automation and one cloud services) creating a complex system, while users face the consequences. We've made commitments to clients who share our disappointment.
I'm in a similar position. I'm not in favor of the cloud function for [product_name] version [version_no]. I partly regret purchasing this version solely for the cloud feature.

I'm grateful that [company_name] has provided such powerful tools. Currently, [product_name] works well on local networks. I hope the engineering team will eventually deliver a better cloud solution or a new platform.
Sending a [product_name] project to AWS: none of the buttons work, no communication occurs.

Update for everyone: with support from [company_name] teams in multiple countries, my cloud deployment issue was identified. The problem is in how AWS Access Keys are copied from the .csv download; extra spaces at the end of either key string cause silent failures. If pasted directly, the system fails without error messages. Upcoming [product_name] versions will address this with error alerts or by ignoring trailing spaces, and documentation will be improved accordingly. Special thanks to the support team for their persistence.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are struggling to enable connectivity between their [product_name] applications and devices via AWS cloud, although local functionality is intact. Troubleshooting efforts spanning region alignment, software versions, and configuration did not resolve the primary issue: cloud connections repeatedly fail with no valuable error feedback. Documentation and official support are seen as lacking, leading users to community troubleshooting, often without success.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate a straightforward and reliably documented process to achieve cloud connectivity between [product_name] and AWS, inclusion of all standard input functions, a fully functional cloud interface, and active, knowledgeable support from the vendor in case of connectivity or deployment problems.
